description:
New US intelligence indicates that Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington, DC, even as officials continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute such a plot, according to seven US officials.

Sources familiar with the latest intelligence characterized the Iranian planning as, for now, an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack. In a statement, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said that the US is “monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.”

The complaint, submitted last week to the House and Senate Armed Services committees and first reported by CBS, comes as Democrats are poised to launch wide-ranging investigations into the Trump administration and its handling of the Iran war when they take control of Congress in January. 

And retired Admiral James Stavridis shares how the face of war is changing, and the impact drones are having on the battlefield. 

Also, Matthew Schmidt, Associate Professor of University of New Haven shares his perspective on the latest Ukrainian drone strike on Russia.

description:
President Donald Trump said Monday “I don’t take any responsibility” for Friday’s nationwide aviation ground stop, blaming the Biden administration and demanding more money from Congress, saying Friday’s failure was caused by “very, very old equipment that had a heart attack.”

Recriminations over the nationwide ground stop are escalating, with the Trump administration shifting blame and demanding tens of billions more in funding while newly empowered congressional Democrats warn there will be no blank check. Key questions include what caused the shutdown and whether it could happen again, especially with the traditional mass exodus at Thanksgiving looming; whether the White House has a plan and the capacity to fix the issue; how much will it cost to address; and how long it will take before a new system comes up to speed.
